flagged.title: Chapters 1-4: Mystery & Terror
flagged.reason: The video presents an invented quotation ('I can be rid of Mr Hyde… whenever I choose' instead of 'the moment I choose, I can be rid of Mr. Hyde') as an exact phrase, which teaches incorrect textual evidence and causes students to fail lesson knowledge checks.

mark_affecting.quote: I can be rid of Mr Hyde… whenever I choose.

flagged.title: Chapters 5-8: The Unravelling
flagged.reason: F9 is mark_affecting because the video explicitly attributes Jekyll's two months of reform, the 'animal within me' metaphor, and the involuntary park-bench transformation to Chapter 5 (which is actually the incident of the letter, while the reform is Chapter 6 and the confession is Chapter 10), directly causing students to fail the lesson's knowledge check.

mark_affecting.quote: Chapter 5 kicks off with Dr Jekyll appearing to reform... after the horrific murder of Sir Danvers Carew, Jekyll totally swears off his potion. For two whole months, he's back to his charity work... Then, sitting on a park bench in January... he transforms...

flagged.title: Character Analysis
flagged.reason: Utterson is incorrectly identified as a 'reliable narrator' (a term explicitly presented as vital for exams), which misleads students on narrative voice and structure (AO2) since the novella is third-person narrative focused through him, not narrated by him.

mark_affecting.quote: This brings us to a vital literary term you really need for your exams: the reliable narrator. Because Utterson has such a highly rational, objective legal mind, he functions as our reliable narrator

flagged.title: Key Themes & Exam Technique
flagged.reason: The video incorrectly teaches that AO4 (written accuracy) is assessed on the 19th-century prose question, causing students to be marked wrong on the lesson's knowledge check, and gives an incorrect quotation ('whenever I choose' instead of 'the moment I choose').

mark_affecting.quote: AO1 is your response using solid quotations. AO2 is all about your analysis... AO3 is how smoothly you weave in that context... and AO4, that's your written accuracy.
